subject.title: Remote gateway node pairing broken — node token scopes empty, approval flow incomplete

question: For remote Node Mode, should device role approval remain separate from gateway-owned node command trust with better UX/recovery, or should the gateway/client bridge approvals or scopes so remote nodes become usable after device approval?
rationale: The remaining symptoms involve remote node execution authorization, token scopes, node approval namespaces, and rotation authority; automation cannot safely choose that boundary from source inspection alone.

options.title: Preserve Split Trust Boundary
options.body: Keep node device approval and node command-surface approval separate, but make the tray/CLI recovery path explicit and prove remote pairing end-to-end.

options.title: Bridge Device Approval To Node Usability
options.body: Change gateway/client behavior so an approved node role can receive usable trust or scopes automatically, accepting a broader remote authorization contract that needs security sign-off.

options.title: Track Gateway Policy Separately
options.body: Limit this repository to clearer Windows diagnostics and route token scope, request namespace, and node-role rotation behavior to the gateway issue.

recommendation.title: Preserve Split Trust Boundary
recommendation.body: Keep node device approval and node command-surface approval separate, but make the tray/CLI recovery path explicit and prove remote pairing end-to-end.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the partial client hardening PR and already framed which Windows-client parts were fixed versus which remote/gateway behaviors remain.
